title: Daily Brain #002: three claims, right or wrong?
notes: Checked by hand. Claim 1 is RIGHT: 10% of 50 = 5 and 50% of 10 = 5; in general x% of y = xy/100 = y% of x. It is right on purpose, so viewers cannot win by always answering 'wrong'.
Claim 2 is WRONG: $80 is 80% of the original, so original = 80 / 0.8 = $100 (check: 100 − 20% = 80). Adding 20% back gives 80 × 1.2 = 96, because 20% of $80 is $16, not $20.
Claim 3 is WRONG: 100 × 1.5 = 150, then 150 × 0.5 = 75, which is 25% below the start. The drop is taken from a bigger number than the rise.
Second solver: a different model, given only the three claims, judged them right / wrong / wrong.
The claims are labelled 'Claim #n', not as anyone's answer: no AI and no statistic is implied.

scenes.title: Daily Brain #002: Spot the mistake
scenes.question: Right or *wrong*?

claim.text: 10% of 50 is the same as 50% of 10.

scenes.narration: Three claims. Easy: ten percent of fifty equals fifty percent of ten. Right or wrong?

why.text: x% of y = y% of x, *always*

scenes.narration: Right. Both are five. It always works.

scenes.title: Daily Brain #002: Spot the mistake
scenes.question: A shirt costs *$80* after a *20% discount*.

claim.text: So it was $96 before. Just add the 20% back.

scenes.narration: Medium. Eighty dollars after twenty percent off. Was it ninety-six before?
Twenty percent off one hundred is eighty. Adding twenty percent back to eighty adds only sixteen.

scenes.title: Daily Brain #002: Spot the mistake
scenes.question: A price goes *up 50%*, then *down 50%*.
scenes.narration: Hard. Up fifty percent, then down fifty percent. Back where it started? Pause if you need to.
One hundred, up half: one fifty. Down half of one fifty: seventy-five.
What's your score out of six?
